cityWatch.text: Bengaluru South civic teams have been told to clear exposed cables, repair damaged footpath slabs and remove waste in J.P. Nagar.

lead.headline: HIJACK THREAT NOTE FORCES BENGALURU–LUCKNOW FLIGHT TO TURN BACK
lead.deck: A handwritten note found in the aircraft lavatory prompted a precautionary return to Kempegowda International Airport; all 178 passengers were deboarded for checks
paragraphs: An IndiGo flight from Bengaluru to Lucknow returned to Kempegowda International Airport after a passenger found a handwritten threat note in the aircraft lavatory late Saturday.
The aircraft landed back at Bengaluru as a precaution. The 178 passengers were deboarded while security teams carried out checks; the airport activated its standard emergency response.
The airline said it followed security procedures. Authorities were examining the aircraft and the note; no confirmed suspect or finding had been announced in the report.

image.alt: IndiGo aircraft returned to Bengaluru after a threat note was found onboard
image.caption: The flight returned to Bengaluru as a precaution. Photo: NDTV

sidebarStory.headline: MINTO HOSPITAL TREATS FIRST CRACKER INJURY OF THE SEASON
sidebarStory.subhead: A six-year-old boy suffered a chemical injury to his right eye while watching a bijli firecracker, doctors said
paragraphs: Minto Eye Hospital reported its first cracker-related injury of the season after a six-year-old boy sustained a grade-two chemical injury to his right eye on Friday. He is receiving treatment.

groups.ariaLabel: Bengaluru enforcement, public support, and jobs news

stories.headline: ED SEARCHES COINDCX AND DELTA EXCHANGE OFFICES
paragraphs: The Enforcement Directorate searched three Bengaluru premises linked to CoinDCX and Delta Exchange on November 4 and 5 over alleged unauthorized cross-border transactions involving crypto derivatives and tokenized foreign stocks. The companies said they cooperated with officials; CoinDCX said customer funds and operations were safe.

stories.headline: OVER 52,000 SUSPENDED PENSIONS RESTORED IN BENGALURU URBAN
paragraphs: The district administration restored pension benefits for 52,632 beneficiaries after reviewing suspended applications, Deputy Commissioner said. The review covered about 6,700 cases in Anekal; officials cited technical issues and income-threshold checks among the reasons for suspension.

stories.headline: BIAL SAYS KANNADIGAS FORM MAJORITY OF ITS WORKFORCE
paragraphs: Bengaluru airport operator BIAL said Kannadigas make up a majority of its workforce and that airport expansion is creating local jobs. The statement followed a Karnataka Rakshana Vedike request for more employment for local residents; BIAL did not provide workforce figures in its response.

groups.ariaLabel: India air quality, reservation, and Ladakh news

stories.headline: GRAP III CURBS IMPOSED AS DELHI AIR TURNS SEVERE
paragraphs: Delhi recorded an air quality index of 382 on Friday, its worst pre-Diwali reading in eight years, according to the report. The Commission for Air Quality Management invoked Stage III measures across the National Capital Region, including restrictions on some construction and vehicle use.

stories.headline: SALARY ALONE CANNOT DETERMINE OBC CREAMY-LAYER STATUS: SC
paragraphs: The Supreme Court clarified that salary income alone cannot determine whether an OBC candidate falls within the creamy layer; parents’ service category is relevant under the applicable rules. The ruling will not reopen completed selections or promotions. The Court said it applies to the still-incomplete allocation process for the 2025 Civil Services Examination.

stories.headline: WANGCHUK ALLEGES ONLINE SMEAR CAMPAIGN BY LADAKH L-G OFFICE
paragraphs: Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk alleged that the Ladakh Lieutenant Governor’s office was behind an online campaign targeting him and his schools, and appealed to the President for intervention. The report said there was no immediate response from the L-G office; the allegation has not been independently established.

groups.ariaLabel: Karnataka recruitment, voter registration, and city services news

stories.headline: KUMARASWAMY SEEKS POSTPONEMENT OF KPSC RECRUITMENT EXAMS
paragraphs: Union Minister H D Kumaraswamy called for postponing KPSC recruitment examinations, including the November 15 test for 319 KAS posts, citing alleged irregularities. Investigations are underway; the report described a demand to defer the tests, not a decision to postpone them.

stories.headline: CEO SENDS DUPLICATE VOTER-ID CASES FOR VERIFICATION
paragraphs: Karnataka’s Chief Electoral Officer said cases involving duplicate EPIC numbers after the voter-roll revision arose from application-processing situations, including multiple Form 6 submissions and pending transfers. The cases have been referred to election officers for verification and corrective action.

stories.headline: BENGALURU SOUTH ORDERS CABLE CLEARANCE AND FOOTPATH REPAIRS
paragraphs: During a Ward One inspection in J.P. Nagar, Bengaluru South officials directed agencies to remove unauthorized and exposed cables, repair damaged footpath slabs and clear roadside waste. The civic drive is intended to improve pedestrian safety and public spaces.

groups.ariaLabel: India under-19 cricket and Bengaluru weather news

stories.headline: INDIA MEET PAKISTAN IN UNDER-19 ASIA CUP TODAY
paragraphs: India face Pakistan in the Under-19 Asia Cup group stage in Al Amerat on Sunday, with the match scheduled to begin at 10:30 a.m. IST. Both teams won their opening matches; a victory would put the winner in a strong position in the group.

stories.headline: PARTLY CLOUDY SKIES FORECAST; NO WARNING TODAY
paragraphs: The India Meteorological Department forecast partly cloudy skies in Bengaluru on Sunday, with a minimum temperature of 20°C and a maximum of 29°C. No weather warning is in effect for the city.
